web_title: 7. Why the Price Is What It Is: Valuation, Reverse DCF & Peer Comps
book_title: 7. Why the Price Is What It Is: Valuation, Reverse DCF & Peer Comps
question: What operating growth and cash-flow conversion does the $142.39 close price in, and how does Bloom compare with listed peers?

epigraph.quote: Our year-to-date performance and customer demand give us confidence to raise our 2026 outlook for the third time this year. [3]
epigraph.author: Simon Edwards, Chief Financial Officer

web_blocks.html: At the November 20, 2026 close, Bloom Energy still carries a demanding growth multiple despite a steep selloff. The market-facts ledger records a close of $142.39 [57]. That is down 15.30% on the day and 29.49% below the November 12 close of $201.93 [42][57]. TradingView reports a consolidated close of $142.45, just six cents above Yahoo Finance [55][57]. On 295.54 million basic shares, equity value is $42.10 billion ($42.12 billion on TradingView), and Finviz enterprise value is $42.43 billion [55][56]. Including 324.289 million Q3 diluted shares and $295 million of net debt-like obligations lifts diluted enterprise value to $46.47 billion [2][57].

Management's October 22 release lifted FY2026 revenue guidance to $4.4 billion to $4.6 billion, or $4.5 billion at the midpoint [3]. Against that guidance, Bloom trades at 9.43 times basic enterprise value and 10.33 times diluted enterprise value [3][56]. Trailing multiples remain high at 10.99 times TTM sales ($3.83 billion), 88.21 times TTM earnings, 68.36 times EV/EBITDA, and 95.84 times free cash flow [55][56]. A 26.70 times forward P/E looks cheaper only if rapid margin gains hold [56].

Nine-month 2026 filings show why headline profit does not equal cash. Revenue reached $3.052 billion and GAAP net income hit $521.523 million, yet operating cash flow was $272.895 million [2]. Subtracting $231.310 million of cash PP&E purchases leaves $41.585 million, or 1.36% of sales ($15.008 million after $26.577 million in affiliate investments) [2]. Our Pass 1 audit found three added drags. A one-time $37.2 million tariff refund ($35.5 million collected) turned adjusted post-capex cash flow negative (-$20.5 million to -$22.2 million) once excluded, right before 10% to 12.5% tariffs arrived in July 2026 [2]. Specific reserves tripled accrued warranty to $70.267 million, and $306.5 million of Oracle warrant assets will cut future recognized revenue [2].

rows: 10.99x TTM P/S; 9.43x basic EV / FY26E mid
web_blocks.takeaway: Historical ratios multiply year-end closes by annual diluted weighted-average shares and divide by annual revenue to set a rough band. Even after dropping 29.5% since November 12, Bloom's 10.99x trailing P/S sits above every year-end mark from FY2021 through FY2025.

web_blocks.html: Five-year multiples show how far expectations remain above past norms. From FY2021 through FY2024, Bloom traded between 2.36 times and 3.91 times sales while posting GAAP losses [1][29][30][31]. Re-rating began at 10.32 times sales in FY2025 as AI data-center power demand surged [1]. Even down 59.47% from its $351.28 high, Bloom still trades above its FY2025 multiple [56][57]. Meanwhile, long-term take-or-pay supplier commitments stand at $5.8 billion against just $661.2 million of long-term product and installation RPO [2].

web_blocks.caption: BE against listed power and data-center infrastructure comparables — November 20, 2026 snapshot [55][56]
web_blocks.takeaway: Cummins, GE Vernova, and Vertiv are adjacent power and data-center equipment comparables rather than pure-play fuel-cell peers. Bloom still commands 88.21x trailing earnings and 21.78x book value versus 16.84x to 31.09x P/E across these three peers, while all four stocks sit in Stage 4 downtrends.

web_blocks.html: Comparing peers shows how much cash conversion Bloom must still prove. Cummins trades at 16.84 times earnings and 4.15 times book with a 12.16% operating margin [55]. GE Vernova trades at 18.35 times earnings on 16.82% revenue growth [55]. Vertiv grows sales at 35.27% with a 20.91% operating margin at 31.09 times earnings [55]. Bloom's 110.59% trailing sales growth is faster, yet its 88.21 times P/E and 21.78 times book value assume clean, lasting free-cash-flow conversion.

web_blocks.the_number: Base-case 10-year DCF value is $75.98 per diluted share. Probability-weighted expected value is $76.17 per diluted share versus the $142.39 close ($142.45 TradingView) [2][3][57].
web_blocks.how_calculated: We project ten years of sales from the $4.5 billion FY2026 midpoint and ramp FCF margin linearly from 1.36% to each case's terminal margin. We discount cash flows and terminal value, subtract $295 million of net debt-like obligations, and divide by 324.289 million diluted shares [2][3].
web_blocks.the_inputs: Starting sales ($4.5B), starting FCF margin (1.36%), net debt-like obligations ($295M), and diluted shares (324.289M) come from filings [2][3]. Bear (40%: 12% CAGR, 6% margin, 12.0% WACC, 2.5% g), Base (45%: 20% CAGR, 12% margin, 10.0% WACC, 3.0% g), and Bull (15%: 30% CAGR, 18% margin, 10.0% WACC, 3.0% g) are analyst cases; Bull uses the same 10.0% WACC as Base rather than a lower rate on a 4.19-beta equity.
web_blocks.the_range: Values span $13.50 in Bear, $75.98 in Base, and $243.88 in Bull. Terminal value drives 62.3% of Bear enterprise value, 76.1% of Base value, and 79.8% of Bull value. Stressing Base alone drops value to $38.13 at a 6% FCF margin, $39.74 at 12% revenue CAGR, and $53.24 at 12.0% WACC.
web_blocks.if_off: At 10.0% WACC and 3.0% terminal growth, $142.39 per diluted share requires 25.24% annual sales growth for ten years ($42.72B in 2036) at a 15% FCF margin, or 28.19% growth ($53.92B) at 12% margin. Failure to collect $858.6M in contract assets, cover $5.8B in supplier commitments, or curb dilution (344.652M shares with converts/PSUs) pulls fair value toward $11.99–$38.13 [2].

web_blocks.caption: Ten-year DCF scenarios, Base downside stresses, and probability-weighted per-share values (USD) [1][2][3]
web_blocks.takeaway: Equalizing Bull WACC to 10.0% prevents a lower discount rate from inflating expected value ($76.17), which sits 46.5% below the $142.39 close. Base stresses to a 6% FCF margin ($38.13), 12% CAGR ($39.74), or 12.0% WACC ($53.24) confirm severe downside if execution slips.

web_blocks.html: Reverse-DCF math shows why a 29.5% pullback has not created a value entry. On Finviz's $42.43 billion basic EV, a 15% Year-10 FCF margin at 10.0% WACC requires 24.04% annual sales growth to $38.80 billion by 2036 [56]. On diluted EV ($46.47 billion), the hurdle rises to 25.24% growth ($42.72 billion), or 28.19% growth at a 12% margin [2]. Only our Bull case ($243.88 at 10.0% WACC) clears $142.39. That path demands 30% annual growth for ten years without margin drag from Oracle warrants, vendor advances, or gas turbines [1][2].

book_paragraphs: A falling stock price is not automatically a bargain. Between November 12 and November 20, 2026, Bloom Energy fell nearly 30 percent, closing at $142.39 on the market-facts ledger and $142.45 on TradingView. That slide trimmed basic market cap from nearly $60 billion to $42.10 billion, with Finviz enterprise value near $42.43 billion. Including 324.289 million diluted shares and $295 million of net debt-like obligations puts diluted enterprise value near $46.47 billion. Against the $4.5 billion FY2026 revenue midpoint, the market still pays 9.4 to 10.3 times forward sales.

Nine-month 2026 filings show why cash flow lags GAAP income. Bloom posted $3.052 billion in revenue and $521.523 million in net income, yet operating cash flow was $272.895 million. Subtracting $231.310 million in PP&E purchases left $41.585 million before $26.577 million in affiliate investments. Excluding a one-time $37.2 million tariff refund ($35.5 million cash collected) turns adjusted post-capex cash flow negative (-$20.5 million to -$22.2 million) before $157.641 million in stock compensation. New 10 to 12.5 percent tariffs arrived in July 2026, warranty reserves tripled to $70.267 million, and $306.5 million of Oracle warrant assets will reduce future sales.

Historical sales multiples confirm that valuation risk has only moderated. From FY2021 through FY2024, Bloom's year-end price-to-sales proxy stayed between 2.36 times and 3.91 times during recurring losses. AI power demand pushed that ratio to 10.32 times at year-end 2025. Even down almost 60 percent from its $351.28 high, Bloom's 10.99 times trailing sales still exceeds every year-end mark of the prior five years.

Peer multiples reinforce the gap. Cummins trades at 16.84 times earnings, GE Vernova at 18.35 times, and Vertiv at 31.09 times. Bloom trades at 88.21 times trailing earnings and 21.78 times book value. Faster sales growth justifies part of a premium only if that growth turns into clean cash flow without warranty surprises or customer defaults.

Our ten-year DCF puts exact numbers on that bar without distorting the discount rate. Starting from $4.5 billion of FY2026 sales and a 1.36 percent FCF margin, Bear (12 percent growth, 6 percent margin, 12 percent WACC) yields $13.50 per diluted share. Base (20 percent growth, 12 percent margin, 10 percent WACC) yields $75.98. Using the same 10 percent WACC for Bull (30 percent growth to $62 billion in sales and an 18 percent margin) yields $243.88 instead of an artificially subsidized figure.

Weighting those cases at 40 percent Bear, 45 percent Base, and 15 percent Bull gives $76.17 per diluted share, sitting 46.5 percent below the $142.39 close. Stressing Base alone drops value to $38.13 at a 6 percent FCF margin, $39.74 at 12 percent growth, or $53.24 at a 12 percent discount rate. In reverse, $142.39 on diluted shares requires over 25 percent annual revenue growth for ten years at a 15 percent terminal FCF margin. With $5.8 billion in take-or-pay supplier commitments ahead of $661.2 million in long-term RPO, the stock offers no margin of safety.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
book_callouts.text: A 30 percent drop feels cheap only if you anchor to the old high. On cash flow, Bloom at $142.39 still demands 25 percent annual growth for ten years just to break even on diluted DCF math.
